items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawns are marching on the kingside. Which move starts White's play on the queenside?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Nb5, c5.
Rb1 is worse than the best move by at least 40 centipawns.

hints: Look at the pawn on c4 and the knight on c3. Which of them can start play on the side where Black has no pawns?
The two best queenside moves are a knight jump and a pawn break.
The knight goes to the b-file, or the c-pawn moves to the fifth rank.
items.explain: Black's pawns are on the kingside, so White's counterplay is on the queenside. The knight jump and the c-pawn break are rated within 0.3 pawns of each other. Other plans, such as a kingside pawn move, are also close to level here; the point is to pick a plan [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.c1b1: A rook move that starts neither plan: the engine rates it at least 0.4 pawns worse than the knight jump or the break.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on f4 attacks the bishop on e3. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Bf2.
Bxf4 is worse than the best move by at least 630 centipawns.
After the retreat one white piece (the bishop) attacks a7.

hints: Count: if the bishop takes on f4, what can recapture?
The bishop can retreat along the same diagonal it came from.
It retreats to f2, next to the king.
items.explain: The retreat keeps the bishop on the diagonal f2-a7, where it watches c5 and a7. Capturing on f4 would lose a bishop for a pawn [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.e3f4: Taking the pawn loses the bishop to the recapture exf4 for one pawn; the engine rates it at least 6 pawns worse than the retreat (about 7 at depth 16).

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn has just captured on c5 and now attacks b4. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers bxc5.
Bxc5 is worse than the best move by at least 380 centipawns.
After the recapture one white pawn (on c5) attacks d6.

hints: Which white pieces can capture the pawn on c5?
One of them is a pawn, and a pawn on c5 would attack d6 again.
The b-pawn captures toward the centre.
items.explain: The b-pawn recaptures, keeps the bishop on f2 and puts a pawn on c5 that attacks d6 again [V, depth 16: bxc5 first].

feedback_by_move.f2c5: The pawn on d6 attacks c5, so the bishop would simply be captured; the engine rates this at least 3.8 pawns worse than the pawn recapture (about 4.5 at depth 16).

items.prompt: Black to move. The queens are off, but Black still has the kingside pawns. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers g4.
Rd7 is worse than the best move by at least 40 centipawns.
After the move one black pawn (on g4) attacks f3.

hints: Count the black pawns on the right side of the board and the squares in front of them.
A pawn move next to the f4 pawn attacks a white pawn.
The g-pawn advances one square.
items.explain: The pawn on g4 attacks f3, so White must trade it or lose control of the kingside squares. The engine rates the break a little ahead of the quiet rook move (about half a pawn; depth-16 readings move by a few tenths), which fits Black's plan since move 12 [V, depth 16].

feedback_by_move.g7d7: A rook move that leaves the pawn storm unused; the engine rates it at least 0.4 pawns worse than the break (about 0.5 at depth 16, inside the noise of a few tenths).

items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight has just captured the pawn on c5. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers b4.
Nd3 is worse than the best move by at least 80 centipawns.
After the pawn move two white pieces (the pawn and the bishop) attack c5.

hints: The knight on c5 stands on a square White's pawns can attack.
A pawn on b4 would attack c5.
The b-pawn moves two squares.
items.explain: The pawn on b4 attacks the knight, so Black must spend a move rescuing it while White's queenside pawns advance for free [V, depth 16: b4 first].

feedback_by_move.e1d3: A natural-looking knight move that also attacks c5, but it leaves the pawn on b2 at home; the engine rates it 0.8 pawns worse than the pawn move, which wins time on the knight.

items.prompt: Black to move. The white pawn on b4 is attacked by the knight on a6. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Nh4, Nb8.
Nxb4 is worse than the best move by at least 50 centipawns.
Only one white piece (the queen) attacks, and so defends, the pawn on b4.

hints: Count the white pieces that defend b4. What does the capture cost if the queen takes back?
Only the queen defends b4. After Nxb4 Qxb4 Black has given a knight for one pawn.
Two quiet knight moves are best: one retreats the knight, the other attacks something on h4.
items.explain: The pawn on b4 is defended once, by the queen on a3. Capturing it and losing the knight for one pawn needs a very fast attack, and the engine says the attack falls short [V, depth 16]. The two quiet knight moves are rated about equal.

feedback_by_move.a6b4: The capture gives a knight for a pawn after the queen recaptures; the engine rates it 0.5 pawns worse than the two quiet knight moves.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on h5 clears the way for a pawn break. Which pawn move makes the thematic King's Indian break?

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers f5.
c5 is worse than the best move by at least 120 centipawns.
After the move one black pawn (on f5) attacks e4.

hints: Which pawn break does Black want in the King's Indian?
The break attacks the pawn on e4.
A pawn on the f-file moves two squares.
items.explain: The pawn on f5 attacks e4 and begins the kingside play. It also leaves the e6 square without a pawn guard, which is why White's knight heads there [V, depth 16: f5 first].

feedback_by_move.c7c5: The pawn on c5 would be attacked by the b-pawn and simply lost; the engine rates it at least 1.2 pawns worse (about 1.4 at depth 16) than the thematic break.

items.prompt: White to move after ...f5. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Ng5.
exf5 is worse than the best move by at least 90 centipawns.
From g5 the knight attacks e4, e6, f3, f7, h3 and h7.

hints: Look at the squares e6, f7 and h7. Which white piece can reach a square from which it attacks them?
A knight move eyes all three.
The knight goes to the fifth rank on the g-file.
items.explain: The knight on g5 attacks e6, f7 and h7 and eyes the weak squares behind the f5 pawn. It also attacks e4, so it helps defend the pawn [V, depth 16: Ng5 first].

feedback_by_move.e4f5: Taking on f5 lets Black recapture with the knight or bishop at no cost; the engine rates it 0.9 pawns worse than the knight move.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on e4 is attacked twice. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers f3, Bf3.
b5 is worse than the best move by at least 40 centipawns.
After the pawn move one white pawn (on f3) attacks e4, supporting it.

hints: Count the black attackers of e4 and the white defenders: the pawn is attacked twice and defended twice.
A pawn move can add a defender; so can a bishop move.
One move is the f-pawn advance, the other brings the bishop to f3.
items.explain: Black attacks e4 twice (pawn f5 and knight f6) and White defends it twice (Nc3 and Ng5), so the exchange on e4 would be level. The pawn on f3 or the bishop on f3 adds a third defender for safety and keeps the centre closed. The engine puts them within 0.2 pawns of each other [V, depth 16]. Game C went with the bishop.

feedback_by_move.b4b5: A queenside pawn move that ignores the pressure on e4; the engine rates it 0.4 pawns worse than the two moves that support e4.

items.prompt: White to move. The knight on g5 is attacked by the pawn on h6. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Ne6.
Nh3 is worse than the best move by at least 270 centipawns.
From e6 the knight attacks c5, c7, d4, d8, f4, f8, g5 and g7.

hints: Do not retreat first: look at what the knight can attack from e6.
From e6 the knight attacks three heavy or valuable pieces at once.
The knight goes to e6.
items.explain: The knight on e6 attacks the queen, the rook on f8 and the bishop on g7 together, so Black must capture it; White's pawn recapture then leaves a far-advanced pawn on e6 [V, depth 16: the only good move].

feedback_by_move.g5h3: The retreat is safe but passive; the engine rates it at least 2.7 pawns worse (about 3.3 at depth 16) than the knight trade on e6.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on f3 attacks the bishop on e2. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Bd1.
Rae1 is worse than the best move by at least 200 centipawns.
One black pawn (on f3) attacks e2.

hints: Count the squares the bishop on e2 can retreat to.
Only one retreat keeps the bishop protected and in touch with the kingside.
It goes to d1.
items.explain: The pawn on f3 attacks e2 and g2, so the bishop has to move. The retreat to d1 is the only reasonable answer; the engine rates the alternatives far lower [V, depth 16]. Black's pawn on f3 now cramps White.

feedback_by_move.a1e1: Leaving the bishop to be captured loses it for nothing; the engine rates this 2.0 pawns worse than the retreat.

items.prompt: Black to move. Choose a move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers Qxe6, Nc6.
Qxc4 is worse than the best move by at least 160 centipawns.

hints: Which capture leaves the queen where a bishop move can hit it with tempo?
Check what each white piece attacks after the capture. One capture keeps the queen near the king.
The queen takes the pawn on e6, or the knight develops to c6.
items.explain: Taking on e6 wins the strong white pawn and keeps the queen near the king; developing the knight is rated almost equal. The capture on c4 pulls the queen away and allows White to gain tempi against it; depth 16 puts it clearly worse [V].

feedback_by_move.c8c4: The pawn on c4 looks free, but the queen leaves the king and walks into tempo-gaining moves; the engine rates it at least 1.6 pawns worse (about 1.9 at depth 16) than the two good moves.

items.prompt: White has just played Nb5. Tap the three squares in Black's camp where the knight attacks a pawn.

claims.statement: From b5 the knight attacks a3, a7, c3, c7, d4 and d6.
Black's pawn stands on a7.
Black's pawn stands on c7.
Black's pawn stands on d6.

hints: A knight attacks the squares one knight jump away.
Look at the pawns on the a, c and d files that sit a knight jump from b5.
The pawns on a7, c7 and d6.
items.explain: From b5 the knight attacks a7, c7 and d6, the squares behind Black's pawn chain. That is the purpose of 14.Nb5: it makes Black spend a move on ...a6 to chase the knight away [V: attack squares checked by rules].
